facts.fact: For theft of luggage in a running train, approach the train conductor/TTE, coach attendant, guard or GRP/RPF escort, who give the FIR form; fill it and hand it back and it is forwarded to the police station, so the passenger need not break the journey
facts.quote: They will give the FIR Form which may be duly filled in and handed over to them. The complaint will then be forwarded to the Police station for necessary action.. The passenger need not break his journey to lodge a complaint with the police.

facts.fact: The passenger can also approach the RPF Assistance Posts at major railway stations for help in lodging the complaint
facts.quote: The passenger can also approach the RPF Assistance Posts at major railway stations for any assistance in lodging the complaint.

facts.fact: Crime on the railways (such as theft) is registered and investigated by the Government Railway Police (GRP)/District Police, so the complaint can also be made at the GRP police station
facts.quote: State Governments are responsible for prevention, detection, registration and investigation of crime and maintenance of law and order on Railways through their law enforcement agencies viz. Government Railway Police (GRP)/District Police.

facts.fact: Rail Madad helpline 139 can be called for all security-related assistance
facts.quote: All India Rail Madad Help line number 139 may be called for all security related assistance.

facts.fact: On 139, option 1 is for security or medical assistance
facts.quote: 139 – Integrated Helpline · Security Helpline or Medical Assistance ( 1 )

facts.fact: For immediate assistance passengers can complain on the Rail Madad portal or through helpline 139, which is integrated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) number 112
facts.quote: For immediate assistance, passengers can make complaint on Rail Madad Portal directly or through Helpline Number 139 [integrated with Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) No.112].

facts.fact: Complaints can be lodged on the Rail Madad website (railmadad.indianrailways.gov.in) or the Rail Madad app
A stolen mobile phone can be reported through Rail Madad (online or 139); RPF uses the DoT CEIR portal to block and trace it
facts.quote: Passengers can report lost or stolen mobile phones through the Rail Madad platform, either online or by dialling 139. If they choose not to file an FIR, they will be guided to register their complaint on the CEIR portal.

summary: All facts confirmed: FIR form via TTE/guard/GRP-RPF escort (Railway Board FIR note, CR theft-of-luggage page), RPF Assistance Posts, GRP, Rail Madad 139 (option 1, ERSS 112), Rail Madad portal/app, CEIR for phones.
